**Resubmitted — T4C: deviation, preferred-level cure (validated ok:true).**

What changed in response to the verifier:

- **Operative repair to the convenience grant.** 14.2.2 now tracks the playbook's model construction directly: *"PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ, in which case SFJ will refund to PB, pro rata, any amounts prepaid by PB for the period after the effective date of termination."* The intervening "at any time" that separated "for convenience" from the notice period has been dropped, so the grant, the 30-day written-notice trigger and the pro-rata refund read as one continuous, ungated permission rather than a qualified one.
- **Vendor bar retained as-is.** New 14.2.11: "SFJ shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Term." No survival tail, expense language or procedure added.
- **Minimality and intent unchanged.** Only the $60M funding gate, the pre-first-Regulatory-Approval window and the redacted notice period are deleted; the 300% Development Cost payment, Trial Data Package mechanic, Approval Payment continuation, Section 6.2 adjustment and Section 6.7 Buy-Out credit remain verbatim. SFJ's event-triggered exits (14.2.3, 14.2.6, 14.2.10) survive, and Section 5.2.2.2's reference to 14.2.10 is not disturbed.
- **Noted, not drafted:** the 300% payment now attaches to a convenience exit at any point in the Term. That cap sits only at the fallback, so it stays out of the preferred-level edit and is offered in the comment; if the fallback is taken up, notice must move into the 60–90 day band and an express three-months-of-fees cap must replace the 300% formula in operative text.
